restatements.text: Repeals the state law that requires cities to allow up to two homes on single-family lots, returning the authority to set the number of homes allowed on residential lots to individual cities.

findings.quote: Each city sets the number of homes allowed on each residential lot.
findings.mechanism: Replaces a state density mandate with local discretion over residential zoning limits.

findings.quote: The state requirement to allow two homes per single-family lot is repealed.
findings.mechanism: Removes the statewide rule that ensures duplexes or second units can be built on single-family lots, allowing cities to ban them.

analysis.answer: Current law requires cities to allow up to two homes on any single-family zoned lot without a public hearing. The measure repeals this state mandate, leaving the authority to set residential limits entirely to individual cities.
The measure may impose an opportunity cost on property owners who lose the ability to build a second unit if their city chooses to restrict density.

Incumbent residents who prefer lower density and local control over neighborhood character benefit. Prospective renters, buyers, and property owners who wish to add units bear the cost of a potentially constrained housing supply.
Cities facing pressure from existing residents are likely to restrict lots to a single home, reducing the construction of duplexes and accessory dwelling units in those jurisdictions.

The measure addresses the perceived problem of state overreach overriding local zoning preferences. The mechanism directly removes the state mandate. In doing so, it removes a state-level policy meant to address housing shortages, potentially allowing cities to reintroduce local barriers to new housing.
City councils, local planning departments, and neighborhood groups gain power over residential density rules, at the expense of state lawmakers and property owners.

gain.empty_reason: The measure shifts authority and removes state guarantees rather than directly advancing any of the listed concerns.
